dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine, how can I help you this morning?

Good morning, señora. My name is Wilson Lopes. I am calling from 3 Wellington Avenue, in the Fifth Ward, near the corner. I am sorry to bother you again, but I must report that our basement has flooded. Again. This is the second time this winter.
Oh, Mr. Lopes. I think I spoke with you a couple weeks ago, didn't I? About the drain on the corner there?

Yes, yes, I believe it was you. In the evening, on a Tuesday. And earlier that same day, our tenant, Miss Lombardozzi, she called also. She rents the upstairs apartment. We both called, señora. We both said the same thing. And now look.

Okay. Let me pull it up. Three Wellington Avenue... yes, here it is. So I've got your first call from Sunday the eleventh, then the crew came out Monday the twelfth, and then the two calls on the thirteenth. Okay. Tell me what happened this time.

With this storm, the snow that came Sunday and then became rain, and it only stopped this morning. Overnight, Sunday into today, the water came into the basement. The same places as before. The back cellar door, and the basement windows. Exactly the same. Nothing different. And this time it is deeper. About five inches. The first time, it was three.
So overnight Sunday into Monday, water came in through the back cellar door and the basement windows, about five inches. And the first time was about three inches.

That is correct. And with respect, señora, I want to be very clear. When the crew came on the Monday, the twelfth, they cleaned the grate. They took out some dirt, some silt, from around the top. That is all. They did not look underneath, under the street. I told you this on the phone that Tuesday. Miss Lombardozzi told you this. The drain still was backing up. And nobody came after that. Nobody called. Two weeks.
I hear you. I do have a note here that it was flagged for a supervisor to take a look after those calls on the thirteenth.

Flagged, yes. You told me this. But excuse me, what does it mean, flagged, if no one comes? I waited. My husband waited. We thought, okay, they will call, they will tell us something. And instead the next storm comes and the water comes in again. Worse.
That's fair. I'm not going to argue with you on that. I'm sorry it happened a second time.

Thank you. I appreciate. But I must ask you something. Please, I do not want this to be written down like a new problem, like it is the first time, like it is bad luck. It is the same corner, the same drain, the same door, the same windows. This is a pattern, señora. It is not one time. I would like that the city treats it like that.

Understood. I'm going to log this as a repeat backup at the same location, and I'll reference the earlier calls and the crew visit right in the notes so anybody who opens it sees the whole history. Not a new, separate thing.
Good. Thank you. That is what I want.
And what got wet this time? Same stuff as before, or anything new?

The same. We have boxes down there, the school things of our kids, papers, old notebooks. Those got wet again. We had dried what we could from the first time, and now, again wet. And the spare refrigerator, it was standing in the water again. Nothing new was damaged, only those things. But, señora, the same things two times. You understand.
Boxes of the kids' school things and the spare refrigerator, wet again, nothing new affected. Got it.

Also I want to tell you, it is not only my house. My neighbors, the next two houses, they had water in their cellars also. I spoke with them this morning, outside, while we were all pumping. All three houses. So this is not about my door or my windows. It is the drain.
The next two houses over had water in their cellars as well?
Yes. Both of them.
Okay, that's helpful, actually. I'm putting that in. Three houses in a row with water helps make the case it's the line and not just one property.

That is what I have been saying since the beginning. [pause] Excuse me. I am trying to be patient. Today I have no route. I drive a school bus, and this morning there is nothing for me, so I am home, and I have spent the morning in the basement with the pump and the wet vac instead. I am a little tired, I am sorry.
No, don't apologize. You've had a morning.

So I would like to ask, please. Not again a crew to clean only the grate. I would like a supervisor, or an engineer, someone who knows the pipes, to come and look at this drain properly. Under the street. Because cleaning the top, we already saw, does not fix it.

Okay. So I'm going to do two things here. First, I'm booking a crew to go out to the corner, and I'm writing in the notes that the grate and basin top were already cleared on the twelfth and it backed up again, so they need to go into the line itself, not just the surface. Second, I'm requesting a supervisor call you back directly, and I'm putting in that you're asking for a supervisor or an engineer to look at the drain.
When will the crew come?
Let me look at the board. [pause] Okay, everybody's out on storm cleanup today and tomorrow, as you can imagine, but I can get them to you Wednesday. Wednesday the twenty-eighth.
Wednesday. And the supervisor?
I'm putting the callback in for by Thursday, the twenty-ninth. That's the request I'm sending.
With respect, señora, last time also there was a request. I would like to know this time somebody will really call.

I get it. What I can tell you is I'm marking it as a repeat flood with neighbors affected, and that does get it looked at differently than a first call. And if Thursday comes and goes and you haven't heard anything, you call back and ask for me, Lorraine, and I'll walk it over myself.
Okay. Okay. I will do that. I hope I will not need to.
Me too. What's the best number for the supervisor to reach you?
My cell phone. 401-555-0132. It is also the number of my husband, it is the same, so if he answers he will know about this.
401-555-0132. And your name again, just so I have the spelling right, Wilson, W-I-L-S-O-N, Lopes, L-O-P-E-S?
Correct. Lopes with S at the end.

Perfect. So let me read this back to you. Three Wellington Avenue. Basement flooded a second time this winter, overnight Sunday into Monday the twenty-sixth, about five inches, through the back cellar door and the basement windows, same as the first flood on the tenth. Boxes of school things and the spare refrigerator wet again, nothing new. The next two houses also had water in their cellars. You're asking for this to be treated as a pattern and for a supervisor or engineer to look at the drain. Crew Wednesday the twenty-eighth, supervisor callback by Thursday the twenty-ninth. Did I miss anything?
No, that is everything. Thank you for writing it all. Only, please, if you can put also that the crew last time cleaned only the top. I want them to know before they come.
It's in there. First line of the notes.
Thank you, señora. I am sorry if I was a little hard. But two times in one month, and we called, and we called. You understand.
I do. You weren't hard. Go get some rest if you can, and try to get things dried out down there.
I will try. We will keep the pump running. Thank you, Lorraine. Have a good day.
You too, Mr. Lopes. Take care.
